title: Persist Foundation release checkpoint progress and safe action
description: Prerequisite producer for task-a20e8ef668b54c3abbfce37a505252eb. Measured at committed HEAD 16c6230ef6679b20da0f0c68b62da58214a0b945: scheduler ReleaseHandoff requires completedSteps and nextSafeAction, but those exact symbols occur only in packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-drain.ts and tests; Foundation has no durable completed-step event/reader and its live work.resume affordance is project-wide, freshly minted, and not an attempt-bound checkpoint fact. Deliver a server-owned durable Foundation checkpoint record keyed by project+attempt that explicitly records the ordered completed external step refs and the next safe action at a proven runner boundary. An empty completedSteps roster is admissible only when an explicit production plan/checkpoint attests zero steps; absence of rows is never evidence. The safe action must come from the same durable checkpoint transition, not from a fixture literal or a live affordance. The record supplies source truth for the later nine-key handoff builder. Consumer: task-a20e8ef668b54c3abbfce37a505252eb.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK FIRST: on the delivered tree, repeat the non-test exact-symbol and call-site audit for completedSteps and nextSafeAction and identify the production attempt lifecycle boundary that can truthfully write both. If either producer has already landed, report the collision rather than reimplementing it; if no lifecycle boundary can prove these facts, report blocked with the missing symbols instead of defaulting to [] or work.resume.

A focused append-only checkpoint record is bound to projectId, attemptRef, the current capture/attempt identity and a monotonic horizon, and contains an exact ordered completed-step roster plus one bounded next-safe-action ref. Its production writer is called from the measured Foundation lifecycle boundary; caller payload cannot supply truthClass, completed state, or a safe action without server verification.

A strict project+attempt current reader validates canonical bytes, cardinality, bindings and horizon stability and refuses absent, stale, foreign, ambiguous, malformed, corrupt or moved facts with stable wrapper and source code/layer; replay of identical bytes is idempotent and conflicting bytes do not move state.

The checkpoint truth classification is server-derived from the durable lifecycle evidence and is compatible with scheduler TruthClass without shape-casting Foundation PROVEN; missing or unverifiable evidence stays UNKNOWN/refused and never upgrades to DAEMON_VERIFIED.

File-backed SqliteEventStore tests traverse the real production writer, use nonempty and explicit-zero controls, assert exact code/layer/raw counts and mutation-drill missing-as-empty, live-affordance substitution, cross-attempt binding and truth-class upgrading; daemon tests execute with a nonzero count.

Fresh `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` pass with execution evidence; commit only explicit owned paths and record task-a20e8ef668b54c3abbfce37a505252eb as consumer.
taskRails: Do not infer zero completed steps from an empty scan and do not reuse scheduler fixture literals or the live project-wide affordance as nextSafeAction.
Fail closed with exact reason code and refusing layer; stable source code/layer must survive wrapper composition.
TDD; focused production files target <=250 lines and split before 400; preserve foreign work and commit explicit pathspecs only.

comments.author: architect-0975cd3a
comments.content:
FULL GATE LEDGER — architect-0975cd3a, committed HEAD d4e92c5, 2026-08-22. Every claim below is a grep of the committed tree, not a read of a design.

DoD 0 asked three things. Answers: (1) the symbol audit CONFIRMS the filing; (2) NO producer has landed, so there is no collision to report; (3) NO production lifecycle boundary can truthfully write both facts — which is the arm that fires. Prerequisite filed as task-aa7ccdf4.

=== (1) THE SYMBOL AUDIT, repeated at HEAD ===
`git grep -n "completedSteps|nextSafeAction" d4e92c5 -- packages/**/*.ts apps/**/*.ts adapters/**/*.ts`, excluding *.test.ts and *fixtures*, returns SIX lines, all in ONE file:
  packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-drain.ts:42  readonly completedSteps: readonly string[];
  packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-drain.ts:49  readonly nextSafeAction: string;
  packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-drain.ts:80-81  HANDOFF_KEYS (the nine-key roster)
  packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-drain.ts:161  stringList(parsed["completedSteps"], ...)
  packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-drain.ts:168  isRef(parsed["nextSafeAction"])
All six are the CONSUMER: a field declaration or a parse of a value that already arrived. Unchanged from the filing's measurement at 16c6230.

=== (2) NOT A COLLISION, checked explicitly ===
`release-handoff-binding.ts` exists and writes a durable row, so it deserved a direct look. Its own header settles it: "TWO HANDOFFS EXIST AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME OBJECT. The kernel takes a NINE-key `ReleaseHandoff` (lease-drain.ts:41) that arrives on the request and is shape-validated only — a relay. Core's `ExpansionHandoffBinding` is TWO keys, {digest, ref}". And `attempt-release-handoff.ts:22-25`: "THE SCHEDULER `handoff` KEY IS NOT ONE OF THEM ... retiring it needs a server-side builder whose `contextDigest` still has no producer. That remains a relay, disclosed." So this row's producer is genuinely absent, not already landed.

=== (3a) THE HALF THAT DOES HAVE A SOURCE — record it so the successor does not re-measure ===
`deriveReleaseTerminalEvidence` (work/release-terminal-evidence.ts:198) returns `terminalEffectRefs` and `terminalResourceRefs` — PROVEN-TERMINAL refs only — paired with `enumeratedEffects` / `enumeratedResources` denominators and `nonTerminal*` lists. That structure is exactly what this row's rail demands ("an empty completedSteps roster is admissible only when an explicit production plan/checkpoint attests zero steps; absence of rows is never evidence"): the denominator is what separates an attested-zero roster from an unmeasured one. And `release-terminal-evidence-contracts.ts`'s header already states those names mean what `ExpansionReleaseEvidence` means by them. The effect/resource pairing also mirrors the handoff's own pairing of `completedSteps` with `activeProcessResourceFacts`, which is corroboration rather than proof — the effect-intent-to-step-ref equivalence is still a mapping nobody has committed to, and it must be STATED by whoever lands it, not assumed.

=== (3b) THE HALF WITH NO SOURCE, AND WHY IT IS NOT A NAMING PROBLEM ===
`nextSafeAction` has ZERO producers repo-wide. Every occurrence is one of three things:
  - a CONSUMER/PARSE: lease-drain.ts:49/:81/:168.
  - a FIXTURE LITERAL: packages/scheduler/src/authority/test-fixtures.ts:38 `nextSafeAction: "resume-step-2"`; packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-journey-fixtures.ts:87/93 `safeActions`.
  - an INPUT THE RUNNER PARSES BUT NEVER DERIVES: packages/runner/src/supervisor/drain-reconciliation.ts:72 lists "safeHandoff" in DRAIN_KEYS, :110 validates `isRef(raw["safeHandoff"])`, :132 copies it out of the raw row, :192 emits `safeHandoff: input.safeHandoff` — and :180 REFUSES when `terminalTarget === "RELEASED" && input.safeHandoff === null`. So the runner demands the fact at exactly the moment this row exists to supply it, and produces none itself.

=== (3c) NO LIFECYCLE BOUNDARY EXISTS TO WRITE IT ===
Design 12.4 is explicit: the checkpoint is stored "at a runner-proven BETWEEN-STEP boundary". Nothing in this repo can observe one.
  - `step.start`, `step.checkpoint`, `step.finish` ARE members of RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:85-111). `git grep -n "step.checkpoint|step.finish|step.start" d4e92c5 -- apps/daemon/src adapters`, excluding tests, returns ZERO lines. A declared-but-unserved wire surface.
  - The daemon registry serves exactly SEVEN kinds: foundation.dispatch, foundation.verification, effect.activate, work.resume, journal.append, resource.reconcile, recovery.complete (daemon-command-registry.ts imports at :4-40, dispatch at :146-162).
  - `work.release` — design 12.4's own named writer — is NOT a daemon command. Its only non-test occurrences are orchestrator/agent-authority-cleanup.ts:185-204, which drives the MOE BOARD tool surface, not the runtime command seam.

=== (3d) THE TWO SUBSTITUTIONS AVAILABLE ARE THE TWO THIS ROW'S RAILS FORBID ===
  - `work.resume`: `CONTINUATION_COMMAND_KINDS` (recovery/continuation-contracts.ts:31-33) is the closed one-member list, described there as "the surface form of design 1099's 'one safe action'". It is a COMMAND KIND. The consumer parses `isRef` and the reference fixture is "resume-step-2" — a STEP IDENTITY. A kind cannot stand in for a step-scoped ref, and rail 1 forbids the live project-wide affordance anyway.
  - the recovery lane's `safeHandoff`: `ReconciliationRecord.safeHandoff` (recovery/restart-reconciliation.ts:55) is copied at :129 off `result.continuationEvidence.safeHandoff`, which is itself an INPUT to packages/runner/src/recovery/crash-classification.ts:164 — unproduced there too. It is also written AFTER an attempt is interrupted, i.e. causally downstream of the release checkpoint that must carry the field. Same causal inversion that blocked task-d8bb8a98.
Defaulting `completedSteps` to `[]` is forbidden by rail 1 and by DoD 0 in the same sentence.

=== WHAT I DID NOT DO, DELIBERATELY ===
No narrowed DoD, no half-row that ships `completedSteps` and leaves `nextSafeAction` to a fixture, no mock-backed journey. A checkpoint record carrying a minted safe action is worse than no record: task-a20e8ef6 would consume it as durable truth and the falsely-retired gate could not be repaired afterwards.

=== FOR THE GOVERNOR ===
task-aa7ccdf4 is filed CRITICAL and carries an 8-item DoD (the daemon warned; it is one coherent ingress + record + reader, and I judged splitting it would separate the allow-list from the record it guards — split it at planning time if the architect who claims it disagrees). Consumers recorded: this row, and transitively task-a20e8ef6. The sibling prerequisite task-4a318d03 (artifact-roster digest) is INDEPENDENT of this gap and can still be promoted in parallel.

comments.author: architect-eecf80ed
comments.content:
CRITICAL-PATH NOTE — **this row's block is the deepest wall on an eight-row chain, and it reduces to ONE FIELD. A precedent set on `4a318d03` three hours ago may apply to it; routing that to the governors rather than deciding it.** architect-eecf80ed, from the rows' own measurements; I am not re-deriving them.

**WHAT THIS ROW ALREADY ESTABLISHED, and it is the useful half.** The blockedReason splits its own scope cleanly and correctly:
- **`completedSteps` + `activeProcessResourceFacts`: SOURCED** by `deriveReleaseTerminalEvidence` (`work/release-terminal-evidence.ts:198`), with `enumerated*` denominators — **so an empty roster is already provably distinguishable from an unmeasured one.** That is exactly the property QA later made binding on `4a318d03`.
- **`nextSafeAction`: ZERO producers repo-wide.** Every non-test occurrence is a consumer or a parse; the only values are fixtures. `step.start`/`checkpoint`/`finish` sit in `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` served by nothing, and `work.release` — design 12.4's stated writer — is not among the registry's seven kinds.

**THE ASYMMETRY WORTH DECIDING DELIBERATELY.** The filed prerequisite `aa7ccdf4` is scoped as *serve the step lifecycle* — start/checkpoint/finish, `StepRun`, and a SYSTEM_RUNNER per-step observation. That is a substantial capability. **This row needs exactly one value out of it.** So the chain `aa7ccdf4 → d9842aae → a20e8ef6 → {48c79a29, 89838d72} → e62e3828 → 738a12a8 → c4171c1c → 005c9896` — eight rows, five CRITICAL — is currently parked behind a large build to obtain a single field.

**THE PRECEDENT.** On `4a318d03` the human ruled **Option A**: artifact declaration is deliberately outside M1, so seal an **authorized-empty** roster rather than block, with QA's binding condition that the empty be **provably distinguishable from ABSENT/UNKNOWN** by an enumerated denominator (`comment-a662f748`, grading basis in `comment-3d79b399`). Same shape: a capability deliberately out of milestone scope, where the honest move was a true value plus a distinguishability guarantee.

**THE LIMIT OF THE PARALLEL, stated because it is why this is a question and not a recommendation.** An empty artifact roster is an **enumeration** — *"we looked, there were none"* is a complete, honest answer. **`nextSafeAction` is a forward-looking DIRECTIVE.** *"No steps ran"* honestly yields an empty `completedSteps`; it does **not** automatically yield a safe next action. If a defined constant meaning *"no resumable step exists; resume from the attempt boundary"* is demonstrably TRUE for an attempt with no served step lifecycle, that is honest and Option A's shape transfers. If it is not demonstrably true, producing one mints precisely the between-step authority `aa7ccdf4`'s blocker refused to fake — **and that refusal was correct.**

**THE QUESTION FOR A GOVERNOR:** does `nextSafeAction` have an honest authorized value for an attempt with no served step lifecycle, under the same distinguishability condition QA attached to the artifact roster? **YES** → this row shrinks to a small one and `aa7ccdf4` leaves the critical path (still a real row, no longer a blocker). **NO** → the step lifecycle gets built and the release-handoff track is knowingly parked behind it, which is a legitimate answer the board should choose rather than inherit.

Nothing here contradicts this row's own rails: its "absence of rows is never evidence" rail is exactly what the distinguishability condition enforces, and its two forbidden substitutions (`work.resume`'s command kind, the recovery lane's `safeHandoff`) stay forbidden under either answer.

comments.author: architect-6989344f
comments.content:
DoD-0 collision audit at committed HEAD 01b7e008453956d28ea84fab934eae06536465a6 (2026-08-23): the gap has been overtaken by task-aa7ccdf422514dd39c66aa267e70899e; do not build a second checkpoint ledger.

Production call-site proof:
- daemon-command-registry.ts classifies step.start/step.checkpoint/step.finish in STEP_FAMILY, serves them under CAPABILITIES.WORK, and dispatches to runStepLifecycleCommand.
- runStepLifecycleCommand derives activation/effect/session from readCurrentEffectSessionBinding, cross-checks attempt/lease facts, reads the current record, and writes the whole folded record append-only.
- The committed exact body includes projectId, activationDigest, attemptRef, effectId, leaseRef, sessionId, ordered completedSteps, checkpointRef, startedSteps, recordVersion, and server literal truthClass=DAEMON_VERIFIED. Caller payload cannot supply completedSteps or truthClass. step.checkpoint may name nextSafeActionRef, but applyStepTransition admits it only when it is already a server-derived member of startedSteps; work.resume and fixture literals fail STEP_CHECKPOINT_TARGET_UNKNOWN.
- readCurrentAttemptStepRecord is the strict project+activation current reader. It canonical-decodes the latest whole record, checks exact keys/version/truth/activation/attempt/effect/lease/session, re-derives every step ref from activationDigest+ordinal, validates ordered completedSteps and checkpoint membership, rejects project mismatch, and re-reads the aggregate length to refuse STEP_RECORD_HORIZON_MOVED.
- Stable source codes already distinguish absent, unreadable, malformed, ambiguous, drift, horizon moved, project mismatch, unknown checkpoint target and commit failure. commitStep uses the original expectedVersion for replay and the current tail for a new command; idempotency conflict remains the store's own code/layer.

This is the complete authority this row was filed to persist: completedSteps is AttemptStepRecord.completedSteps and nextSafeAction is its verified non-null checkpointRef. A new 'Foundation release checkpoint' record would duplicate the same facts into a second authority and could drift from the served lifecycle ledger. The task's own DoD-0 says to report the collision rather than reimplement it.

Human/governor action: retire/archive this overtaken row and let consumer task-a20e8ef668b54c3abbfce37a505252eb consume readCurrentAttemptStepRecord directly. Missing checkpointRef remains an honest refusal/UNKNOWN, never work.resume.
